discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 271050
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
550 AM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Occasional light rain, possibly mixed with a little wet snow
  at times this morning, is expected to continue and then 
  diminish from west to east this afternoon into early evening. 
  Snow accumulation is not expected at this time.

- Another round of rain late Saturday night into Sunday evening
  followed by blustery/windy conditions behind a cold front for
  Sunday night into Monday.

- The coldest conditions are expected Monday followed by a
  warming trend. The next chance of rain will be late in the
  work week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 237 AM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

A broad negative mid/upper level negative height anomaly will 
slowly track northeast today into northeast CONUS. Stronger 
upper dynamics are favored well southeast of the local area, but
residence time of this negative height anomaly is being 
prolonged locally by tendency of large scale diabatic PV anomaly
to displace the mid level height minimum to the northwest 
across northeast Kentucky/southern Ohio. While best upper jet 
dynamics will continue to shift across Mid Atlantic this 
morning, the separated interior PV anomaly across the Ohio 
Valley will exhibit only slow northeast progression today. This 
should prolong some weak isentropic forcing today, particularly 
across far northeast Indiana/northwest Ohio/south central Lower 
Michigan. Some weak deformation forcing associated with this 
lagging PV anomaly could also enhance precip later this morning 
into this afternoon particularly along and east of the I-69 
corridor. Additional precip chances will exist from western 
Lower Michigan into northwest Indiana tied more to sheared 
vorticity filament on western fringe of this system, where also 
some weak low level frontogenesis will likely play some 
continued role where remnants of a weak TROWAL signature should 
persist into this afternoon.

Increased low level lift since early last evening has likely 
contributed to some weak low level cooling that could raise some 
ptype concerns with indications in higher res near term models of 
925 mb wet bulb temps just below freezing through daybreak. The
complicating factor for realizing any mixing in of wet snow 
this morning will be likely maintenance of sfc wet bulbs just 
above freezing for most areas. Current indications would suggest
that best chance of mixing in some wet snow may be across 
northeast portions of the of forecast area where sfc wet bulbs 
will likely be a bit lower from NE IN into SE Lower MI, and 
where some brief stronger lift with any deformation-forced 
precip, could steer precip types briefly to some wet snow mixing
in during period of strongest lift. Sfc wet bulbs may remain a 
bit higher across the west, although cannot completely rule out 
some brief wet snow mixing in this morning if any axes of 
stronger low level fgen can come into play especially across SW 
Lower Michigan. Forecast thinking from previous cycles remains 
intact in that any snow accumulation would likely only be a 
tenth or two across grassy areas this morning, with roads 
remaining wet. Most areas should not receive any snow
accumulation.

For tonight, lingering light rain may persist for eastern locations 
early evening as last mid level trough axis pushes across the area. 
This will be followed by approach of some induced short wave mid 
level ridging in advance of next upper trough tracking across 
the Upper Midwest. Stronger forcing with this feature looks to 
remain across the central/northern Great Lakes on Saturday, and 
while some mid level moisture is likely to increase with this 
feature Saturday AM, subcloud layer appears to be too dry to 
support mentionable PoPs at this time. Otherwise, some increase 
in sun is expected by PM as mid level clouds push east and 
modest low level warm advection should support some moderation 
in temps back into mid/upper 40s for Saturday afternoon.

Attention will then turn to a digging wave from Pacific NW for 
Saturday night into Sunday. It does appear as though both advective 
and deformation forcing components will accompany this short wave. 
Typically by this time of year, the expected suppressed track 
of low level reflection of this system would support some wintry
precip, but this pattern looks to be characterized by continued
lack of any immediate northern latitude phasing, with push of 
cold air appearing a bit too delayed for anything more than rain
with this system. It is possible at very tail end of precip, 
some wet snow could briefly mix in Sunday evening, but this 
potential appears too low for a mention at this time. Colder and
blustery conditions follow behind the associated cold front for
Sunday night into Monday with Monday likely to feature coldest 
conditions of this period.

Not much change was warranted for the later periods with higher 
confidence in a warmup through the work week and mainly dry 
conditions through Thursday. Medium range models are in general 
agreement of larger scale southern stream wave evolving in split-
flow across western CONUS, eventually leading to better rain chances 
heading into late Thursday/Friday.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 550 AM EST Fri Nov 27 2026

Light rain/drizzle will continue through much of the day as a
large low pressure system slowly exits the region. Some brief
snow may mix in at times early this morning but confidence in
impacts is low and will therefore hold with PROB30 mention.
Ceilings holding slightly higher than guidance but still IFR and
this will persist through most of today. Transition back to VFR
expected 00-03Z this evening. Northerly winds slowly back W/SW
but remain under 20 kts.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 4 AM EST Saturday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili
AVIATION...AGD

SPC AC 270535

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1135 PM CST Thu Nov 26 2026

   Valid 271200Z - 281200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe threat is forecast across the U.S. through tonight.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   At mid-levels, a low will move across the northeastern U.S. today as
   flow becomes west-northwesterly over much of the western half of the
   nation. A subtle shortwave trough will move inland across the
   Pacific Northwest. Isolated thunderstorms will be possible across
   Oregon ahead of the trough this afternoon and evening. Elsewhere
   across the continental U.S., no thunderstorms are forecast today and
   tonight.

   ..Broyles/Halbert-E.. 11/27/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 270659

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1259 AM CST Fri Nov 27 2026

   Valid 281200Z - 291200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorm potential appears low on Saturday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A mid/upper-level shortwave trough is forecast to amplify on
   Saturday as it digs southeastward from the northern Rockies to the
   Ozark Plateau. In response to this system, a surface low will deepen
   across the southern High Plains during the day, before moving
   eastward toward the MO/AR border late in the period. An attendant
   cold front will sweep through the central and southern Plains. 

   Surface-based instability is expected to remain minimal through the
   period. However, modest moistening above the surface beneath cooling
   aloft will allow MUCAPE of 100-300 J/kg to develop late Saturday
   night into early Sunday morning from AR into parts of the MS and
   lower OH Valleys. Within this environment, a strengthening low-level
   warm-advection regime will support development of elevated
   convection capable of producing sporadic lightning flashes. At this
   time, elevated buoyancy appears too weak for an organized-severe
   threat.

   ..Dean.. 11/27/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 270827

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0227 AM CST Fri Nov 27 2026

   Valid 291200Z - 301200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Organized severe potential currently appears low on Sunday, though
   any storms across parts of the Mid-South and Ohio Valley could be
   accompanied by strong wind gusts.

   ...Synopsis...
   A vigorous mid/upper-level shortwave trough is forecast to
   accelerate eastward on Sunday as it moves from the Ozark Plateau
   region across the OH/TN Valleys and into the Mid-Atlantic/Northeast.
   A surface low attendant to this system will deepen as it moves
   east-northeastward across the Ohio Valley towards the Lower Great
   Lakes. A cold front will surge eastward in conjunction with the
   surface low. 

   Low-level moisture return is forecast to remain modest, with 60s F
   dewpoints likely remaining confined to parts of MS/AL, and 50s F
   dewpoints potentially being limited to along/south of the Ohio
   River. Even where surface theta-e is relatively maximized, MLCAPE
   will likely remain relatively meager (generally 500 J/kg or less),
   with little to no surface-based instability expected closer to the
   surface low track. 

   Despite the general lack of buoyancy, strong ascent will aid in the
   development of low-topped convection along the front, with
   prefrontal showers also expected. Aside from potential early-day
   elevated convection, lightning activity may remain rather sparse,
   due to the weak instability.

   Deep-layer wind fields will be strong, and generally intensify
   through the period as the primary shortwave trough accelerates
   eastward. Given the strength of the flow (with 45-55 kt at 850 mb
   along/ahead of the front), any robust convection would conditionally
   pose a threat for localized wind damage. However, with low-level
   lapse rates generally expected to remain quite weak where the
   strongest DCVA and frontal surge are expected, potential for
   convectively enhanced severe/damaging gusts remains quite uncertain.

   Most AI guidance generates severe probabilities across some portion
   of this region, but wind-gust forecasts from long-range CAMs (RRFS
   and GSL-MPAS) depict only modest (and generally subsevere)
   convective enhancement to the rather strong near- and post-frontal
   wind fields. Due to the inherent uncertainty regarding strongly
   forced, low-topped convective-wind potential, no 5% area has been
   included at this time. Probabilities may eventually be needed,
   depending on trends regarding heating/destabilization and strength
   of frontal forcing.

   ..Dean.. 11/27/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1930Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
